name: Kodak Sasson digital camera prototype
description: Experimental camera combining electronic image sensing, digitization and magnetic recording of a still image.

date.basis: Date stated by the cited source; see event scope.

events.statement: Sasson recorded a black-and-white image with a Kodak prototype in December 1975.

evidence.supports: Museum identifies Sasson, Fairchild sensor, Motorola conversion, image and cassette.

events.caveats: Internal prototype, not proof of a consumer product or global first.

research.note: Independent reader: Checked the Camera Museum account: the Fairchild sensor is not identified as the represented CCD101, and 23 seconds is recording time, not exposure. The CCD relation is scoped to the general functional concept, not identity of the Fairchild sensor with the original experimental device.

links.statement: The prototype’s CCD imaging uses the charge-transfer device function described in the 1970 concept.
links.caveats: This concerns the general CCD function; it does not identify Boyle and Smith’s experimental device as the specific Fairchild sensor.
